topology: 1 node x4 H100, NVSHMEM put-ring, BOTH providers in one process
why: regression test for provider coexistence (7a5b55a): ib + gpumem loaded into ONE process, both writing into ONE capture. Same workload/topology as 04, the only variable is the second provider — so a coexistence regression shows up here and nowhere else.
scope_note: single-node, so NVSHMEM never posts an IB send (every peer is NVLink-reachable): the ib side contributes entities (MR/QP/modify_qp), not traffic. Cross-transport TRAFFIC correlation needs 2 nodes — see 07_nvshmem_multinode.
workload_note: identical to case 04 by construction — `putget 65536 3` on 4 PEs — because the only variable this case changes is the second provider. Both cases assert the same derivation against the same oracle, which is what makes the comparison between them evidence rather than coincidence.
entity_close_note: CLOSED 2026-08-07 (MN5 job 44372679). Root cause was never a registration door: object-ops hooks are installed INSIDE an ibv_context, and UCX opens contexts through a door this provider does not interpose, so ibv_reg_dm_mr's trampoline was never installed on them while ibv_dereg_mr — a preload hook, context-independent — still fired. Hence closes naming regions nothing opened. Job 44369505 proved it: every unmatched close carried installed=NO. Fixed by installing a context on first sight through ANY door rather than only at ibv_open_device, with ibv_close_device hooked so a recycled context pointer is not mistaken for one already patched — omitting that lifecycle silently cost case 02 two of its eight ranks. Case 02 now records 504 device_memory regions that were entirely absent before, with sends unchanged at 26880. Six registration hypotheses died before one that followed the object instead of the symbol; see plans/PLAN-20260806-2320-dlvsym-interposer-not-observed.

expect_fail_asserts.entity_close_accounted: 30 CQs per rank are destroyed that nothing recorded creating, identically on every rank of case 02 (NCCL) and case 07 (NVSHMEM multinode) — 164 opens vs 194 closes, 1312/1552 per run in both. NOT a defect in the close hook and not a new door: it is the residual of the gap this file's entity_close_note already records, where UCX opens ibv_contexts through a door this provider does not interpose. Measured on MN5 job 44400676. ibv_create_cq is a PRELOAD hook and is live from process start, so a CQ through it is never missed; verbs_context::create_cq_ex is an OBJECT-OPS slot that exists only once the context is installed. PCOMM_TRACE_CTX_INSTALL=1 shows 48 of 73 contexts per rank first reaching us at door=create_cq, i.e. opened somewhere we do not see — so create_cq_ex calls made before that first create_cq hit an unpatched slot and are invisible. PCOMM_TRACE_MR_CALLERS=1 names the destroyer: uct_ib_verbs_destroy_cq in libuct_ib.so.0, cqe=8191. Note its installed=yes is NOT evidence against the window — that flag is sampled at DESTROY time, by which point the context has long since installed at create_cq. IbCompletionQueue.origin confirms create_cq_ex does fire and is worth hooking: 480 of 1312 recorded CQs (60/rank) came through it and would otherwise have been missed too. The fix is to interpose the context-opening door UCX actually uses (mlx5dv_open_device is the unexamined candidate), which is the same shape as the create_qp_ex hunt that cost case 08 a week. Marked xfail rather than weakened, exactly as qp_creation_accounted was on case 08 until its door was found — the rows stay printed.
